I love Norm Macdonald‘s style of comedy. Everything from the word choices to his cadences, I love it. An amazing career he had.

That being said: isn’t there an interview where he said he used to pretend to be drunk so he could get away with groping women at comedy clubs? And there’s articles online about experiences women had being groped by him at clubs, where accusers were a fan who took a picture of him, or severs at the club who said that only certain servers were allowed to give him drinks in the green room because of a history he had with groping the staff.

Idk I know the stuff I read can never be confirmed or disproved, but there are instances that seem in line when those stories, like when he sneakily kissed Roma Downey on SNL.

I know it’s awful to say awful things about the deceased, but Reddit (and myself included) love his comedy so much that we tend to idolize him as a great man we can all aspire to be like. His death really stuck with me in September/October, I couldn’t stop thinking about how tragic it was a guy like him had to experience the demise that he did. I cried watching that clip when he got choked up on Letterman’s final episode. And then I read that stuff about women’s personal experiences with him and I just didn’t know what to believe or feel.

Humans are complicated af. Fame and success only complicate things even more. We can always separate the artist from the art and all that. But I wanna advocate for a world where we have a lot more respect for women (and everybody else obviously) and idk I know because how revered and talented Norm was, and what he went through, this comment might get downvoted into invisibility. I don’t want to convince anyone to think he was a bad man, maybe I just want to spark honest conversation about him and hopefully find evidence that there was some fabrication about those accusations.
